comments.author: Blackhorse311
comments.body_html:
Hey briktor, thanks for the kind words about KSG, I’mglad it’s keeping you in the game!

Good news: this is definitely not a BotMind issue. Since you installed on SPT 4.0.11, the server would have crashed before the mod ever loaded — meaning no BigBrain layers were registered, no configs were changed, and nothing was written to disk. BotMind is completely gone from your system once you delete the plugin folder.

What you’re describing — scavs not engaging, hesitant combat, needing multiple shots to get a response — sounds like a SAIN configuration issue. Here’s what I’d try:

  1. Delete your SAIN config: Remove BepInEx/config/me.sol.sain.cfg and the BepInEx/config/SAIN/ folder (if it exists). SAIN will regenerate fresh defaults on next launch.
  2. Clear BepInEx cache: Delete the BepInEx/cache/ folder — stale cached assemblies can cause weird behavior.
  3. Check your SAIN preset: In F12 → SAIN, make sure you’re on a standard preset and not something custom that may have gotten corrupted.
  4. Nuclear option: If none of that works, try a clean SPT install with just BigBrain + SAIN and nothing else. If bots work normally, add mods back one at a time to find the real culprit.

You don’t need to file a GitHub issue for this since it’s not a BotMind bug — but if you do upgrade to SPT 4.0.12, v1.3.0 just dropped and it’ll work great for you. Good luck!

comments.author: Blackhorse311
comments.body_html:
Yep! when you toggle a module off in F12, it genuinely stops running. Each module’s brain layer checks the F12 toggle as the very first thing it does, and if it’s off, it returns false immediately. No loot scanning, no pathfinding, no logic executes. It’s not just hiding the behavior, the code actually doesn’t run at all.

To narrow down what’s hitting your performance, try this:

  1. Disable all three modules in F12 (Looting, Questing, MedicBuddy) and play a raid as your baseline
  2. Enable Questing only — play a raid and note any FPS difference
  3. Enable Looting only — play a raid and compare
  4. MedicBuddy only runs when you summon it, so it shouldn’t affect baseline performance

Also check if you have the Max Bots Per Map slider set above 0 in the Performance section. If you cranked that up, that adds more bots to the map which is the biggest performance hit in SPT — each bot runs its own AI, pathfinding, and combat simulation. Setting it back to 0 uses game defaults and might be your fix right there. 0 doesn’t mean NO BOTS, 0 means my mod is not adding any bots. (Hope that makes sense. I have a monster rig and I push an extra 31 bots into my games to make it chaotic as all get out. :) )

Let me know what you find!

comments.author: Blackhorse311
comments.body_html:
v1.4.0 is out! 🔧

Big thanks to ExcellentBug, wookie143, Legitimancer, and DigitalB for the detailed reports — this update is directly because of your feedback.

What was wrong:

  • Bots were creeping/walking instead of jogging or sprinting (move speeds were set too conservatively at 0.5-0.7)
  • Bots would stay crouched or slow after switching between AI layers (pose/speed values weren’t resetting)
  • Looting was too aggressive — bots acted like vacuum cleaners, with PMCs and Scavs looting side by side every 2 seconds
  • No breathing room between questing objectives — bots would instantly chain from one to the next
  • Bots would walk right past enemies because SAIN’s detection has a natural delay, and we were only checking SAIN’s combat state (not EFT’s native enemy awareness)

What we fixed:

  • Move speeds bumped up across all modules (now 0.7-1.0 range with proper sprint/jog/walk thresholds)
  • Pose and speed reset to standing/full speed in ALL layer Stop() methods — no more inheriting crouch from a previous state
  • Looting throttled: scan interval 2s → 8s, 15s cooldown between targets, max 3 targets per 2 minutes, default search radius 50m → 35m
  • 5-second cooldown between questing objectives so bots look natural
  • Combat detection now checks BOTH SAIN and EFT’s native enemy detection — catches enemies faster
  • New “Combat Alert Duration” slider in F12 (default 30s) — controls how long bots stay in fight mode before going back to objectives

New stuff:

  • Optional SAIN “BotMind” preset included — tunes detection speed (+50%), aggression (+30%), and hearing (+15%). Press F6 in-game, select “BotMind” preset. Fully reversible.
  • Waypoints mod now listed as recommended — it provides the improved NavMesh data that our navigation relies on. If you’re having bots freeze or get stuck, install Waypoints!
  • Combat Alert Duration is configurable from 10-120 seconds in F12

If you had issues with bots in v1.3.0, please give v1.4.0 a try and let me know how it goes! Download from GitHub: https://github.com/Blackhorse311/BotMind/releases/tag/v1.4.0

If you find any bugs, report them here: https://github.com/Blackhorse311/BotMind/issues

What I think might be happening: when the questing layer activates, it generates random NavMesh waypoints from the bot’s current position. To confirm, I need two things:

comments.author: Blackhorse311
comments.body_html:
Good question! Short answer: SAIN profiles work alongside BotMind, not against it.

SAIN handles combat behavior, detection range, aggression, hearing, vision speed, squad tactics, etc. BotMind adds questing, looting, and MedicBuddy on top of SAIN. When a bot detects an enemy (through SAIN), BotMind automatically yields so SAIN handles the fight. Once the coast is clear, BotMind picks back up with questing/looting.

So a more aggressive SAIN profile (like Twitch Players or Live Like) means bots fight harder and longer, which naturally means less time questing/looting, and that’s totally fine, it’s how it’s designed.

BotMind also ships an optional SAIN preset in the download (sain-preset/BotMind/ folder) that’s tuned for a good balance if you want to try it, just drop it in BepInEx/plugins/SAIN/Presets/ and select it in SAIN’s F6 menu.

comments.author: Blackhorse311
comments.body_html:
Yep! Found the root cause. When bots finish a waypoint, the questing layer was handing control back to EFT’s default brain for 5 seconds as a “natural pause.” Problem is, EFT’s brain walks bots straight back to their spawn point during that gap. So toggling questing off lets looting take over (which doesn’t have this issue), and toggling it back on just restarts the cycle.

Fixed in v1.5.0 — the questing layer now stays active during the pause between objectives so EFT’s brain can’t hijack the bot. Also improved waypoint generation so bots actually find reachable destinations instead of giving up and circling spawn.

Hey Chucknastical! Good timing! I’m uploading v1.6.0 right now which has several questing fixes that should help with exactly what you’re seeing.

Those “Path to target failed” → “Navigation failed - target unreachable” warnings mean the bot tried to generate a waypoint but couldn’t find a valid NavMesh path to it. After 2 failed attempts it gives up on that objective. In v1.5.0, if ALL waypoints failed, bots could end up with nothing to do and just stand there.

v1.6.0 has a fix that specifically blocks non-PMC/Scav bots (Raiders, Rogues, Bloodhounds) from getting questing objectives at all, they were getting waypoints designed for PMCs that didn’t work for their spawn locations. That might be part of what you’re seeing depending on bot types.

A couple things to check:

  1. Do you have Waypoints installed? BotMind’s questing relies heavily on NavMesh data, and Waypoints improves it significantly. Without it, path failures are much more common.
  2. What map are you seeing this on? Some maps (Woods, Interchange) have tricky NavMesh that v1.5.0’s graduated waypoint generation was meant to handle, but there could still be edge cases.
  3. Grab v1.6.0 when it’s up and let me know if the standing-around issue persists!

Also cool to hear you’re running FIKA with a headless client, that’s a solid setup for testing. If you can grab the full BepInEx log after a run with v1.6.0 and the issue still happens, toss it on a https://github.com/Blackhorse311/BotMind/issues and I’ll dig into it.

Post-combat patrol loops: This is a known limitation right now. When bots finish fighting and their original waypoints are used up, new ones generate from their current position. So they end up patrolling the combat area instead of pushing across the map. It’s on my list to improve though! I want bots to pick up longer-range objectives after combat instead of just circling locally.

No big cross-map movement: The current max waypoint range for PMCs is 50-150m, which on a map like Shoreline doesn’t cover the distance between major POIs. Bumping those ranges or adding named POI targeting is something I’m looking at for a near-future update.

Scavs staying local: That’s actually by design! Scav range is 30-100m, so they stick closer to their spawn area like they would in live Tarkov. If you have a suggestion for a selectable change of some sort, I’m all ears!

None of these are bugs per se, more like “phase 2” improvements. The core questing loop is working correctly. It’s my waypoint intelligence that needs leveling up. If you want to file a feature request on GitHub for the cross-map movement stuff, or changes for SCAVs, that’d be great for tracking!

comments.author: Blackhorse311
comments.body_html:
Hey waxparrot! Raid Review indeed souds like a great tool for debugging! I’ll grab it and start using it. Thanks!

“Searching for cover” is actually a SAIN combat state, not a BotMind behavior. BotMind’s layers show up as “BotMind_Questing” and “BotMind_Looting” in the brain readout. When a bot enters combat, SAIN takes full control and BotMind steps aside, so I’m fairly certain what you’re seeing is SAIN’s cover-search getting stuck, not BotMind.

A few things to try:

  1. Check your SAIN version and make sure you’re on the latest release
  2. In SAIN’s F6 menu, look at the cover-search settings. Sometimes tightening the search radius or timeout helps
  3. If you want to confirm BotMind isn’t involved, you can disable both Looting and Questing in F12 (BepInEx config) and see if the same behavior happens. My bet is it will, since it’s a SAIN state

If you want to report the cover-search loop to the SAIN devs, Raid Review screenshots with the brain state would be super helpful for them!

Let me know if that clears things up!

comments.author: Blackhorse311
comments.body_html:
Hey dxjre, glad you’re enjoying the mod!

Good questions all, let me hit them one at a time:

  1. Bots wandering a zone for a while: That’s actually working as designed! When questing is enabled, bots explore areas by visiting 3-7 random waypoints within ~30m of each other before moving to the next objective. With questing disabled, they rely on EFT/SAIN’s default patrol behavior which can look different. The next version (v1.7.0) has some improvements to waypoint generation that should help bots move to more varied areas instead of circling the same zone.

  2. Search Radius: That setting is actually for looting (how far bots scan for loot), not questing/patrol behavior. Changing it won’t affect how far bots wander. There isn’t currently a configurable patrol radius, but it’s a reasonable feature request, so I’ll look into that!

  3. Full backpack = bot stops? Nope! If a bot’s inventory is full, the looting layer just won’t activate (nothing to pick up), but questing/movement continues normally. Bots keep patrolling and doing their thing regardless of inventory space.

  4. FIKA: I think I may change the description to “Confirmed compatible”! You and several other users are reporting that it’s running with FIKA successfully.

Let me know if you have any other questions!

Heads up on SPT 4.0.13 compatibility!

Hey everyone, just a quick update. I’ve been testing BotMind, KeepStartingGear, ForcibleEntry, (and GunSense which is a new mod I’m working on) against the new SPT 4.0.13 and it looks like BSG renumbered a bunch of their internal classes again, which broke a lot of mods across the board. SAIN, BigBrain, and several others are all affected to varying degrees even though they say they are 4.0.13 ready. (There’s problems across the Forge spectrum that I don’t think a lot of mod authors have discovered yet).

I’m actively working on getting all of my mods building clean against 4.0.13 right now. Shouldn’t need any major code changes on our end, just tracking down the renamed classes and updating references.

In the meantime:

  • If you’re staying on 4.0.12, everything works as-is, no changes needed
  • If you’ve already updated to 4.0.13, hold tight. I’ll push updated builds once I’ve confirmed everything is working
  • SAIN users on 4.0.13: SAIN 4.4.0 is failing to load bot settings for every bot type. That’s on SAIN’s side, not ours, so keep an eye on @Solarint’s page for an update

I’ll update this thread once I have confirmed 4.0.13-compatible builds ready. Shouldn’t be long!
